newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-THREE SUSPENDED IN BRAWL-MARRED KINGS-SHARKS GAME.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-THREE SUSPENDED IN BRAWL-MARRED KINGS-SHARKS GAME.

text.p: The National Hockey League on Saturday suspended two players from the Los Angeles Kings and one from the San Jose Sharks for a total of nine games for incidents during a brawl-filled game in San Jose Wednesday.

The Kings will have to do without left wing Matt Johnson for four games and defenceman Rob Blake for two, while San Jose's Tony Granato, a former King, was given a three-game suspension. The suspensions are without pay and all three were also hit with maximum $1,000 fines.
Johnson and Granato were both assessed match penalties at the time of the incidents, given when a referee determines there was deliberate intent to injure.
Johnson was suspended for a flagrant elbow on San Jose's Andrei Nazarov midway through the second period, inflicting injuries that will keep Nazarov sidelined for several weeks.

"Mr Johnson delivered a flagrant elbow to the facial area of Mr Nazarov, which clearly precipitated the multi-player altercations that occurred in the second period," NHL senior vice president and discipline chief Brian Burke said in handing down the suspensions.
"Mr Johnson's actions were deliberate and totally unacceptable," Burke said.
Granato, who recovered from off-season brain surgery to make it back to the NHL with San Jose, whacked his stick at the head of Dmitri Khristich after the final buzzer.
"While his opponent was on the ice and defenceless, Mr Granato delivered several cross-checks to the head area of Mr Khristich which were deliberate and could have resulted in injury," Burke said.
Blake was given a double high-sticking minor for his actions against Shean Donovan with just under eight minutes left in the game.
"As Mr Donovan was about to legally check his opponent, Mr Blake delivered a cross-check to the neck, which was intentional and could have resulted in an injury to Mr Donovan," Burke said.
